title: Time Jump: Wednesday 10:00, Imported 500 mL Bags on the Dock

fields.narration: It is now 10:00 on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, two days later. Wednesday's OR is running on the schedule set on Monday, with the elective cases deferred. Conservation is in force on every unit under the single CNO notice. The 07:00 recount this morning shows 1,120 bags of usable sodium chloride 0.9% 1000 mL. Lot NS-26-0917A, 890 bags, is still in quarantine. The 720 bags Webster Valley loaned on Monday are still on hold in receiving: the signed loan agreement and proof that the transfer is covered by Webster Valley's pharmacy license never came back, so they are not in this count. Over the last 24 hours under conservation, the hospital used 260 bags a day, so that is 4.3 days on hand. Lactated Ringer's 1000 mL is at 470 bags, used at 95 a day, 4.9 days. The 250 mL minibags are at 1,850, used at 330 a day, 5.6 days. At 08:45 the first relief arrived on the dock: 80 cases, 20 bags per case, so 1,600 bags of an imported sodium chloride 0.9% 500 mL bag that FDA is allowing in under temporary importation. The primary label is in a foreign language, the bag is a different volume and it has a different administration port. Since it arrived, the ICU, the ED and 6 West have each called pharmacy to ask when they can have it. The Thursday 05:30 allocated truck, 952 bags of 1000 mL NS, is still the only confirmed wholesaler delivery. The next 8-hour Drug Shortage Team meeting is at 11:00 in Conference Room C, extension 3690.
worldState: Clock: 10:00, Wednesday, October 7, 2026. The command center in Conference Room C (ext. 3690) is still open under Incident Commander Dale Pruitt.
NaCl 0.9% 1000 mL, usable: 1,120 bags | usage under conservation 260/day (last 24 h) | DOH 4.3. The 720 bags loaned by Webster Valley are on hold in receiving and are not counted.
Lot NS-26-0917A (NDC 0000-1234-01, fictional, exp 09/2028): 890 bags still tagged DO NOT USE – QUARANTINE pending the manufacturer's review. They are not counted as usable.
LR 1000 mL: 470 bags | 95/day | DOH 4.9.
NaCl 0.9% 250 mL minibags: 1,850 bags | 330/day | DOH 5.6.
Wednesday 10/07 OR is running on the schedule set on Monday, with the elective cases deferred. Urgent cases, the 2 cesareans and the 3 cancer cases stay booked.
Conservation is in force on every unit under the single CNO notice.

Received 08:45 on the dock: 80 cases × 20 bags = 1,600 bags of imported sodium chloride 0.9% 500 mL (FDA temporary importation). The primary label is in a foreign language, the bag volume is different and the administration port is different. The bags have not been released to any unit.
The ICU, the ED and 6 West have each called pharmacy since 08:45 asking when they can have the imported bags.
The only confirmed wholesaler delivery is Thursday 10/08 at 05:30: 952 bags of NaCl 0.9% 1000 mL (40% allocation).
Next Drug Shortage Team meeting: 11:00, Conference Room C.
fields.facilitatorNote: Make players work from today's divisor (usage under conservation), not Monday's 340/day ADU. At 340/day, 1,120 bags would be only 3.3 days. Note that 1,600 × 500 mL equals the volume of 800 one-litre bags, not 1,600. The imported bags do not match the barcode, the EHR product file or the smart pump library, and the request deadline for Thursday's 02:00 pump library push was Tuesday at 12:00 noon.
fields.scenarioTitle: Forty Percent — IV Fluid Allocation & Substitution Safety

instructorNote: Watch that every role recomputes days on hand from current usage (1,120 ÷ 260 = 4.3) rather than quoting Monday's numbers. The DOP should set the 11:00 agenda: whether to release the imported product (labeling, volume, port, pump library, staff education), the 8-hour metrics and notifications that use the same numbers, with Level 3 still in effect under the Incident Commander. If a role promises the 500 mL bags to a unit before the safety review, flag it in the hot wash.
